content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The bookmark manager specification is ready for review:

- [Specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Validation: all 16 checklist items passed; no unresolved clarifications

The proposed first release is a private, single-user bookmark library supporting save, search, tags, favorites, sorting, editing, archiving, restoring, and confirmed deletion. Collaboration, browser extensions, import/export, and nested folders are excluded.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll proceed to the implementation plan; no code has been written yet.

This looks really solid overall — saving, reopening, searching, tagging, favorites, sorting, editing, archiving with restore, and delete-with-confirmation are all there, and that covers what I mainly want.

One thing I do want changed before I approve: when I paste in a web address to save it, I'd like the app to automatically pull in the page's name (and a short description if it can) so I don't have to type a title myself. Right now the spec says it'll just use the raw web address as the title and that it deliberately won't fetch anything from the destination. For me, "save a bookmark" really means dropping in a link and getting back a recognizable entry without hand-typing the name every time — that's a big part of the convenience. I don't need saved copies of pages or summaries or anything heavy, just the basic title/description grabbed from the link when it's available (with me still able to edit it, and saving still working if the site can't be reached).

Could you adjust the spec so saving auto-fills the title/description from the page? Everything else you've described is what I want.

Updated the [bookmark manager specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md) to require:

- Automatic page-title and description retrieval after entering a valid address.
- Editable auto-filled values that are never overwritten after manual changes.
- Immediate saving even when retrieval is slow, blocked, or unsuccessful.
- The web address as the fallback title and an optional blank description.
- No generated summaries or saved page copies—only published page metadata.

The [quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md) passes all 16 checks. The spec now contains 20 functional requirements and 9 measurable success criteria.

If you approve this revision, I’ll move to the implementation-plan gate.

That covers exactly what I was asking for — dropping in a link now fills in the title and description automatically, I can still edit them, and saving works even if the site can't be reached. That's the convenient saving I wanted, and everything else was already what I had in mind.

The specification looks good to me — please go ahead to the implementation plan.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review.

Core design:

- Node.js 24, TypeScript, React 19, Vite 8, and Express 5 in one deployable process.
- Embedded `node:sqlite` persistence with three tables and transactional writes. [`node:sqlite` documentation](https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/sqlite.html)
- Separate, non-blocking metadata preview with timeout, size limits, redirect validation, public-address enforcement, and DNS-rebinding protection based on [OWASP’s SSRF guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html).
- Node’s test runner plus Playwright 1.61.0 and automated accessibility checks.

Artifacts:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- [Technical research and decisions](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md)
- [API contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [UI behavior contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/ui-contract.md)
- [Quickstart and acceptance guide](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)

content:
Bookkeep is built and ready for review at:

[http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000)

Implemented:

- Automatic editable title and description retrieval
- Non-blocking fallback when sites are unreachable
- Persistent bookmarks, tags, favorites, search, filtering, and sorting
- Editing, archiving, restoring, and confirmed deletion
- Responsive desktop/mobile interface
- SSRF-protected metadata retrieval
- Accessible keyboard-friendly controls and dialogs

Validation passed:

- 8 unit tests
- 5 integration tests
- 9 browser workflow tests across desktop/mobile
- 2 accessibility scans
- 1,000-bookmark performance criterion
- Lint, typecheck, and production build
- [All 59 implementation tasks completed](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md)

I adjusted the technical plan from TypeScript 7 to TypeScript 6 because the current lint toolchain does not yet support TypeScript 7; this did not affect product behavior.

I've had a good look and tried it out myself, and Bookkeep does what I set out to build:

- Saving a link works and it sticks around after reloading; when I leave the title blank it falls back to the web address, and I can fill in a title, description, and tags — with the automatic page details we agreed on, and saving still goes through fine when a site can't be reached.
- Pasting the same link again (even without the "https") warns me and points me to the one I already saved instead of duplicating it, and a bad address is rejected with a clear message while keeping what I typed.
- Searching finds links by title, address, description, and tag regardless of capitalization; filtering by tag and by favorites works, and sorting by newest, oldest, and A–Z all behave.
- Editing updates the entry, archiving moves it out of the main list into the Archive and restoring brings it back untouched, and deleting removes it for good from both views.

This is exactly the private bookmark library I wanted — easy to save links, find them again, and keep the collection tidy. I'm happy with it.
